# A library struct a build emits reaches the output under its own bare name,
# because every backend emits a struct by name. gtk4's `arcTo` takes a
# `draw.Point`, so a drawing with an arc in it promotes that declaration into
# the package -- and a program that declares its own `Point` would then get two
# `type Point struct` in one file, which Go refuses and JS resolves to
# whichever came last.
#
# Renaming is what this wants and is not a rename the promoting pass can make:
# the declaration is shared with the memoized library package, so writing to it
# would reach every other build in the process. So it is reported.
! sngl generate --lang=go --platform=gtk4 --out=out clash.sngl
stderr 'declares struct "Point"'
stderr 'sngl:ui/draw'
stderr 'rename the local one'

# The same program without the local declaration builds, which is what says the
# diagnostic is about the collision and not about drawing an arc.
sngl generate --lang=go --platform=gtk4 --out=ok fine.sngl
exists ok/model.go
grep 'type Point struct' ok/model.go

-- clash.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import draw "sngl:ui/draw"

struct Point {
    label string = ""
}

component main() ui.node {
    var p = Point{label = "x"}

    draw.canvas(width=40px, height=20px) {
        draw.path(cmds=[draw.PathCmd{op = "arcTo", cx1 = 1.0, cy1 = 1.0, x = 2.0, y = 2.0, r = 1.0}], style=draw.CanvasStyle{stroke=color{r=255}})
        draw.canvasText(x=0.0, y=0.0, content=p.label, style=draw.CanvasStyle{fill=color{b=255}})
    }
}

ui.window {
    main()
}
-- fine.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import draw "sngl:ui/draw"

component main() ui.node {
    draw.canvas(width=40px, height=20px) {
        draw.path(cmds=[draw.PathCmd{op = "arcTo", cx1 = 1.0, cy1 = 1.0, x = 2.0, y = 2.0, r = 1.0}], style=draw.CanvasStyle{stroke=color{r=255}})
    }
}

ui.window {
    main()
}
